sentences.text: Brief facts as stated are dated on 05.12.2019, when Dilavar @ Dilvarsab S/o. Husensab Mummanagi was walking by side of road in Amatur village, driver of Tipper bearing registration no.KA-24/9714 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, dashed against him and caused accident.
In the said accident, Dilavar sustained grievous injuries and died.

Claiming compensation on account of his untimely death, his wife and two minor children filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, against owner and insurer of motor vehicle.
3.
On service of notice, respondents appeared and opposed claim petition on all grounds.
Contributory negligence was alleged against deceased.
Violation of policy conditions insofar as driving licence, permit and fitness certificate was also alleged.
4. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and thereafter recorded evidence of claimant no.1 as P.W.1 and employer as P.W.2.
Exs.P.1 to 14 were marked.

On other hand respondents did not lead oral evidence but got marked evidence of Exs.R1 to R.4.
5.

On consideration, tribunal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle by its driver and held insurer was liable to pay compensation of Rs.28,53,000/- with interest at rate of 9%.
Aggrieved by said award insurer has filed appeal on quantum of compensation in MFA no.101861/2022.
While claimants have filed in MFA no.101428/2022 for enhancement of compensation.

6. Sri.S.K.Kayakamath, learned counsel for appellant/insurer submitted that though deceased was alleged to be employee of P.W.2 and earning Rs.18,000/- per month, as per salary certificate Ex.P.14, P.W.2 did not produce muster roll.
Claimant did not produce bank pass to indicate employment and salary.
In absence of same, tribunal ought to have considered notional income.
Since excessive monthly income of Rs.15,000/- per month was considered.
Insurer had filed appeal for reduction.
It is also contended that rate of interest at 9% per annum was excessive and unjustified.

7. On other hand Sri.Hanumant R. Latur, learned counsel for claimants/appellants submitted that deceased was admittedly having driving licence to drive heavy goods vehicle as well as heavy passenger vehicle with driver's batch.
Therefore, he cannot be equated to that of ordinary unskilled coolie.
It was further submitted that apart from consistently pleading employment, claimant had produced salary certificate and also examined employer.
Employer had produced his registration certificate as per Ex.P.13 and also service certificate Ex.10.
Therefore, claimants would be entitled for consideration of higher monthly income and for reassessment of compensation.
On above grounds learned counsel sought for allowing claimants appeal and dismissal of insurer's appeal.

8. Heard learned counsel for both parties, perused impugned judgment and award.
9.
From above submission, both insurer as well as claimants are challenging award on quantum of compensation.

Therefore, point that would arises for consideration is:

sentences.text:
"Whether assessment of compensation by tribunal calls for modification of award as sought for?".
10.

Insofar as monthly income indeed claimants have stated that deceased was working as driver with Vinyasa Constructions on monthly salary of Rs.18,000/- per month and they also produced salary certificate as per Ex.P.14, wherein it is indicated that apart from salary, deceased was being paid bhata of Rs.250 per day.
However during cross examination of P.W.2-employer, it is elicited by insurer that employer had maintained employee's records i.e. wage register and muster roll etc.
But same were not produced.
Even bank pass book of deceased to indicate receipt of monthly income is not produced.
In absence, monthly income has to be assessed notionally.
However, as per Ex.R.4 deceased holding licence to drive motorcycle, light motor vehicle heavy goods vehicle and heavy passenger vehicle.
He also possessed driver's batch.
Considering fact that licence was issued in year 2014 and accident had occurred in year 2019, employment with P.W.2 as stated may not be proper.
However deceased who was holding driver's licence cannot equated with that of ordinary coolie.
In circumstances, by reasonable guess work it would be appropriate to consider monthly income of deceased at Rs.16,000/-.
But tribunal has awarded excessive rate of interest at 9% per annum without any specific reasons.
This Court in case of SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED, RAJASTHAN VS. SMT. LAXMI AND OTHERS reported in 2018(4) AKR 808 has held that rate of interest cannot be more than 6%.

entities.text: SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED, RAJASTHAN VS. SMT. LAXMI AND OTHERS reported in 2018(4) AKR 808
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On recomputation of compensation by considering higher income and reducing rate of interest defference between net compensation calculating till day would not vary much.
Therefore instead of disturbing award by recomputing it would be appropriate to confirm award.
Point for consideration is therefore answered in negative in peculiar facts and circumstances of this case.

Consequently, I pass following:
ORDER a) Both appeals are dismissed.
b) Amount in deposit in insurer's appeal is directed to be transmitted to tribunal for payment.
Insurer is directed to deposit balance compensation, if any within six weeks.
c) Pending applications are dismissed as unnecessary.
